title: Shopska Salad
description: Tomato, cucumber, and pepper under a thick white drift of grated sirene. Nothing is cooked and nothing is complicated, which means the tomatoes have to be worth eating on their own.
notes: Sirene is a firm white brine cheese. Feta is the usual substitute, but rinse it first — feta is saltier and this salad has nowhere to hide it.

steps.text: Slice the onion into thin half moons and leave them sitting in cold water while you cut everything else.
steps.tip: Ten minutes in water takes the burn out of a raw onion without turning it limp. Longer and it starts tasting of nothing.

steps.text: Cut the tomatoes into rough chunks and the cucumbers into pieces of roughly the same size.
steps.tip: Matching the sizes is most of what makes this bowl look like the picture. It is also the only knife work in it.

steps.text: Dice the green pepper and drain the onion thoroughly, shaking off every drop.
Toss it all together with the sunflower oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and most of the parsley.
Grate the sirene over the top in a thick even blanket and finish with the last of the parsley.
steps.tip: The cheese goes on top and stays on top. Tossed through, it dissolves into the dressing and the whole bowl goes cloudy.
